plan: Given my private value of $30, I aim to maximize profit by balancing the bid to win without overpaying. Assuming rational competitors, they might bid close to their values. Bidding slightly below my value, like $25, could secure a win if others undervalue the prize or bid conservatively. If they bid higher, I avoid overpaying. This strategy minimizes risk while offering a chance to win profitably.

Given my value of $28, I aim to bid less than $28 to ensure profit if I win. Assuming others bid near their values, I expect bids between $20-$30. Bidding slightly below my value, around $25, could secure a win without overpaying. This balances winning probability and profit margin.

My value is $22. To maximize long-term profit, I should bid slightly below my value, aiming to win by paying less than $22. Assuming others bid close to their value, I will bid $20. This balances winning potential with profit margin. If others bid higher, I lose nothing. If they bid lower, I win and gain a profit margin of $2 or more.
